title: Disney plans several thousand layoffs, asks some managers to cut costs by up to 20%
content:
Disneyis planning to cut several thousand jobs, people familiar with the matter told CNBC.

Some managers at the entertainment giant have been asked to reduce costs by up to 20%, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly.

It marks the latest round of layoffs since CEO Josh D'Amaro took the reins earlier this year. The update comes after separate plans in April to cutas many as 1,000 employees, predominantly in the marketing department, and in September to cut about300 employees, many in human resources and technology divisions.

Bloombergwas first to report the latest round of layoffs.

Company executives warned of the possibility of more reductions in its August earnings report.

"We remain highly focused on reducing costs across the enterprise to create incremental capacity to invest for growth and are evaluating a variety of levers," D'Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston wrote in anAug. 5 letter to shareholders. "We are mid-stream in this work and will provide future updates on our progress."

Disney introduced plans in August for an early retirement program for some employees.

"This is one of several actions we're taking to reshape our organization, including involuntary staff reductions that have already begun in some areas and will continue into next year," Chief People Officer Sonia Coleman wrote in a letter to employees on Aug. 24.

Disney had about 231,000 employees as of the close of its fiscal year 2025, which ended in September of that year, according to thecompany's annual financial report.

Disney is not the only entertainment company looking to reduce costs.Netflixsaid in a memo last month that it wouldlay off roughly 6% of its workforce.Skydance, the newly combined company of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, is also expected to cut staff in an effort to realize $6 billion in synergies over three years.

Disney will report its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings on Nov. 17.

title: Mining giant joins fight to stop killer toad march across Australia
content: Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,A cane toad yesterdayByDearbail JordanPublished1 hour agoRio Tinto is ploughing millions of dollars into stopping the poisonous cane toad reaching the Pilbara region of western Australia, where the mining giant has a vast iron ore operation.The firm, alongside Curtin University in Perth and others, will spend A$28m (Â£14.5m) building a "toad containment zone" to prevent the pest travelling south.While the cane toad is not a direct threat to Rio Tinto's business, it produces toxins lethal to native wildlife and poses a threat to Pilbara's ecosystem.Rio Tinto has previously faced criticism for destroying two sacred Aboriginal rock shelters in Pilbara which sat above tonnes of iron ore.The decision cost the former chief executive his job, provoked a widespread backlash and saw Rio Tinto commit to rebuilding trust with Indigenous communities.Commenting on the proposed containment zone, Roberta Hunter, a ranger in Australia's Nyangumarta Warrarn Indigenous Protected Area, said: "Cane toads destroy the water and animals."When toads come close to our country, we want to be there to stop them because we don't want the country to be destroyed."The plan is to cut off the toad's water supply by building a barrier across 7,500 sq km (2,895 sq m) of land between the Great Sandy Desert and the Indian Ocean.In drier months, the cane toad needs water every few days to survive.If there are no natural water sources, the toad relies on artificial water points normally used for cattle and irrigation.The funding will be used to stop the toad accessing dams, storage tanks or other ground-level water sources. The five-year project will begin in 2027.A number of native species are at risk if the toad gets into Pilbara. These include the northern quoll, whose numbers have been decreasing, the goanna lizard and the ghost bat.The toads were introduced into Australia in 1935 to control beetles within the sugar cane industry.Image source,Getty ImagesImage caption,The northern quoll is at risk from the cane toad in AustraliaSince then, they have been on a slow march west across the country's northern landscape, according to the Australian government, travelling between 40 km and 60 km a year.There are no predators or diseases that control the toads, which defend themselves using poison.Ben Phillips, a professor at Curtin University, said the toads would reach Pilbara within two decades without action.He said: "The toad containment zone is a once in a lifetime opportunity to stop one of the world's worst invasive species in its tracks and protect the region's unique wildlife."Related topicsRio TintoAustraliaInvasive speciesWestern AustraliaToads

title: Russia confirms new Ukraine peace talks as Melania Trump prepares to host ceasefire meeting
content:
Russia on Tuesday confirmed that peace talks with Ukraine and the U.S. will go ahead next week in Abu Dhabi, while also signaling that a meeting between PresidentsVladimir Putin,Donald Trumpand Xi Jinping to end the conflict was on the table.

Putin aide Vladimir ​Medinsky will serve ⁠as Moscow's chief negotiator ​at the talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, Kremlin spokesman ​Dmitry Peskov told reporters on a conference call, according to Reuters.

Separately, First Lady Melania Trump will bring Russian and Ukrainian representatives to the White House to discuss the local ceasefire in Kherson, the White House said Tuesday.

Monday saw the end of a six-day ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky and surrounding areas in the Kherson region to allow for evacuation of residents, in a pause of hostilities that the White House said was brokered by the first lady.

Ukraine on Monday accused Russia of using the ceasefire toreinforce its military positionsin the city.

The first lady's summit on Thursday will be "an extraordinary moment in American history," the White House said, but did not name the representatives who will attend. Melania Trump will deliver remarks on the Oleshky ceasefire at 11 a.m. ET Thursday, it added.

Peskov also said Tuesday the Kremlin hopes to finalize plans for a trilateral meeting between the leaders of Russia, the U.S., and China in the coming days. The comments follow earlier reports that these countries were planning tonegotiate an end to the warin Ukraine, without Ukrainian PresidentVolodymyr Zelenskyyat the table.

Zelenskyy has said that any negotiations over Ukraine's future must include Kyiv.

"It can be acceptable only when we are at the table of negotiations," he said on Oct. 20, adding that he had discussed the proposal of a three-way meeting between the U.S., China, and Russia to negotiate an end to the nearly five-year full-scale war. "Nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine," he said.

Tensions between the U.S. and Ukraine have mounted over recent weeks amid continued strikes between Moscow and Kyiv, including on civilian and energy targets.

A series of movesby the Trump administration in October raised questions about Washington's reliability as Kyiv's most important military partner.

Tuesday's announcement follows U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff saying late Monday that Washington will mediate Ukraine-Russia peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, focusing on security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian issues.

Witkoff also said that U.S. negotiators will meet European and NATO officials in Brussels this week to discuss post-war security guarantees and Ukraine's reconstruction.

title: Drivers may get compensation offers before car finance saga ends
content: Image source,Getty ImagesByKevin PeacheyCost of living correspondentPublished3 November 2026, 09:45 GMTUpdated 4 hours agoDrivers may be offered compensation from lenders ahead of the next legal battle in the car finance mis-selling saga.Regulator the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) said it would welcome lenders making settlement offers as long as customers were not given a worse deal than under its proposed central scheme.That scheme is facing a legal challenge, to be heard in February, with resulting compensation unlikely to be paid until late next year.But Barclays has confirmed it will make early compensation offers from now, with others expected to follow suit.The FCA said it would still only expect a minority of claimants to be made early offers, with most having to wait for the outcome of next year's court case.Stephen Braviner Roman, the FCA's general counsel and co-lead on the motor finance project, said: "Fair settlement offers could result in some people getting money sooner. It's clear they want the choice."Anyone who wants to wait can, and there's no obligation to agree to the offer. We'll closely monitor firms making offers and expect them to be clear what accepting an offer means."Why drivers will receive payoutsThe vast majority of new cars, and many second-hand ones, are bought with finance agreements. Customers pay an initial deposit to secure the vehicle, then a monthly fee with interest.But millions of drivers who took out a car loan between April 2007 and November 2024 will be entitled to compensation after the loans were mis-sold.They mostly related to when car dealers received commission from lenders, based on the interest rate charged to the customer. These were known as discretionary commission arrangements (DCAs) and customers were often not told about them.Average compensation payouts of about Â£829 are expected to be made related to about 12 million car loans - about 37% of the total number during the period.Car finance compensation payments delayed until next yearPublished4 hours agoCompensation will cost the industry up to Â£9.1bn, including administrative costs. Individual payouts will vary, depending on the degree of harm each driver faced.With huge compensation payouts inevitable, some lenders have already set aside millions of pounds to cover the cost.Barclays has decided to start making compensation payments early, potentially to start clearing the cost off its balance sheet. It pointed out that claimants had already faced "a considerable wait"."By making these early settlement offers, we are giving some customers the option of receiving redress sooner, rather than waiting for the legal challenges and any subsequent FCA action to conclude," said a Barclays Partner Finance spokesperson."Each offer will be calculated using the FCA's redress scheme methodology. We will clearly explain how it has been calculated and what accepting a full and final settlement means, so customers can decide whether accepting the offer is right for them."The lender said claimants would start to be contacted directly "in the coming weeks".But it stressed not all customers whose complaints were acknowledged on or before 1 October 2026 would receive an early settlement offer.Guidelines on whether to accept an offerThe FCA has publisheda factsheet to help drivers,externalwork out whether they should accept early settlements from lenders.It will include a list of lenders who are making early offers, to ensure claimants with other lenders are not scammed.The regulator said lenders will need to be clear with people about what accepting any offer means. This includes:Being able to keep any payment, even if the final settlement under the central scheme after the legal challenges proved to be smallerClaimants would not be able to claim more later if the outcome of the legal challenge meant they would have been paid moreAccepting an offer takes you out of the scheme and stops any further input from the financial ombudsmanThe Finance and Leasing Association, which represents lenders, said: "We want to see consumers receive the fairest outcome in as timely a way as possible and recognise that, in some cases, that may point to early settlement, while in others it may be appropriate to await greater legal certainty."But Kevin Durkin, solicitor advocate and director at HD Law, who represented Marcus Johnson who won his case in the Supreme Court, said he had "real reservations" that fair compensation would be offered."These are only heightened by reports that just a small number of claimants will receive what could be lowball offers. I fear this is crumbs from the table, for some customers who are highly likely to be owed more, while the vast majority will receive no offer at all," he said.The main proposed FCA scheme remains partially suspended, pending legal challenges in February.Consumer group Consumer Voice said the proposed compensation scheme left "too many people short-changed". Three lenders - Volkswagen Financial Services, Mercedes Benz Financial Services, and Credit Agricole Auto Finance - are also challenging the scheme.The UK's Upper Tribunal has agreed to hear legal challenges to the scheme, with a hearing scheduled from 16 February to 3 March.Anyone who is concerned about their car finance deal and has not yet complained can still complain directly to their lender. There is information on the FCA website onhow to complain for free,external.Related topicsPersonal financeMoneyCost of LivingPersonal debtUK banking

title: Brookfield targets $27 billion AI data center at power station. Energy firm Drax surges 8%
content:
Brookfieldis targeting a massive artificial intelligence data center in the north of England, as Europe scrambles to develop infrastructure to support the rollout of AI amid high energy and land costs.

Energy companyDrax Groupsaid Tuesday it has signed an agreement with Brookfield and the asset manager's neocloud platform Radiant to jointly develop an AI data center on the Drax Power Station estate in North Yorkshire. London-listed shares of Drax were up 8.2% in early morning trading.

The project is initially targeting up to 100 megawatts of capacity to be operational from the first quarter of 2028, with an additional 500 MW of capacity brought online between 2028 and 2031. It is then looking to secure more than 1 gigawatt of capacity at the site by an unspecified date.

Brookfield estimates that total investment, including semiconductors, could exceed £20 billion ($26.8 billion), with an initial £2.5 billion investment as part of phase 1.

This is a breaking story. Refresh for updates.

title: U.S. strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island as Vance hopes for ‘negotiated settlement’ with Tehran
content:
The U.S. reportedly carried out strikes against Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday, a U.S. official has told MS Now, as Vice President JD Vance expressed hopes of reaching a "negotiated settlement" with Tehran.

The official called the U.S. strikes "a defensive measure" in response to "Iranians using surface to air missiles against US assets."

The strikes were initially reported by The Wall Street Journal, which added that Washington has been carrying out "limited strikes" against the country in recent weeks.

The military campaign against Iran has been kept quiet on purpose so as not to signal any intention of major combat escalation, the report said, quoting an unnamed official.

Qeshm Island, off Iran's southern coast, is the largest island in the Persian Gulf. Located near the Strait of Hormuz, it has emerged as apotential U.S. targetamid reports that anti-ship missiles, mines, drones and attack craft are being kept there in underground tunnels.

President Donald Trump's administration has been talking down risks of an all-out war with Iran, with Vance being the latest to claim "good progress" in talks with Iran.

"The president and I both feel really good about theprospect of potentially comingto a negotiated settlement," Vance told CNN on Monday.

He added, though, that Iranians are "unpredictable" and Trump retains "kinetic and non-kinetic" options against Tehran. Vance said that Washington has not set any deadline for reaching a peace deal with Iran.

A senior Iranian official told the Reuters news agency on Tuesday that Tehran would respond to U.S. aggression forcefully in the region beyond, as they warned the two countries remained far from reaching a deal.

"The enemy seeks to force the Iranian nation into submission through threats and military action, but they are sorely mistaken, Iran will not submit," the official said.

Qatari mediators reportedly travelled to Tehran on Monday night for talks on a version of the draft U.S.-Iran deal that has been under negotiation for the past eight days.

"Tehran's conditions must be met if the US wants Hormuz reopened," the Iranian official told Reuters, adding that nuclear talks could only start afterwards and that the country would not accept Washington's "excessive demands."

Trump said earlier Monday that the U.S. had to go to war with Iran to stop the country from having "a nuclear weapon," that "we're not going to allow Iran ever to have a nuclear weapon. And they understand that."

Last month, the president had said the U.S. will not attack Iran before the midterm elections, after polls ahead of the ballot showed that support for the war had dwindled, with only31% of Americans supportingthe military action.

Trump told Fox News in an interview Monday night that the U.S. had to take a"little detour"to Iran to stop the country from having nuclear weapons.

The president said that the U.S. has bombed out all of Iran's potential nuclear power, but he might target Pickaxe Mountain next. Located south of Iran's Natanz enrichment plant, Pickaxe Mountain houses an underground nuclear facility.

"We might have to go after Pickaxe, but that's not a big deal," Trump said, adding the U.S. could destroy it in one hour.

On Nov. 1, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio had also said Trump would like to resolve the Iranian war "diplomatically," andprefers not to use military force.

title: North Korea denies links to Binance hack as researchers trace stolen billions
content:
North Korea rejected allegations linking Pyongyang to theestimated$6.3 billionBinancehack, calling the accusation a “grave political provocation,” according to state media.

Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denounced the FBI's attribution of the attack to North Korea-linked hacking group TraderTraitor, YohnapreportedTuesday, citing the state-run Korean Central News Agency.

Blockchain analytics firms including Elliptic and Chainalysis have also linked the attack and subsequent movement of the stolen funds to North Korea-linked actors.

"The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a 'cyber criminal state', claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organization 'supported' by the DPRK was involved in the incident," Kim said, according to KCNA.

She accused Washington of misleading international public opinion by portraying cybercrimes around the world as the work of North Korea.

Separately, BinancesaidTuesday it would begin progressively reopening withdrawals for additional crypto assets across more networks, expanding its phased restoration of services following last week's hack.

The denial comes as blockchain analytics firms trace billions of dollars in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance through thousands of wallets across multiple blockchains.

Elliptic andChainalysissaid hackers linked to North Korea have used increasingly complex techniques to obscure the trail of the funds.

In the first four days after the attack, the hackers used roughly 12,000 wallets across 11 blockchains and conducted more than 40,000 transactions, Ellipticsaid in a reportMonday. The activity appeared highly complex and automated, with an average of one new wallet used every 25 seconds.

Much of the laundering activity initially took place on the Tron blockchain, where stolen funds were distributed across about 7,700 addresses before being moved to Ethereum through cross-chain bridges, according to Elliptic. At least $147 million had been transferred out of Tron through such bridges.

The hackers also used decentralized exchanges to swap stolen stablecoins into cryptocurrencies that cannot be frozen by their issuers, including ether. Elliptic said roughly $786 million in stablecoins was converted before issuers including Tether and Circle froze the remaining assets.

The laundering operation has since expanded to other blockchains, includingSolana. ChainalysissaidNorth Korea-linked actors had begun a new phase of laundering after moving more than $500 million through intermediary wallets on Tron.

Elliptic also identified the first signs of bitcoin mixing, a technique designed to make transactions harder to trace. About 28 bitcoin, worth $2.2 million, had passed through 18 mixing transactions as of early Monday, the firm said.

Despite the extensive movement of funds, about $2.85 billion — or 44% of exactly $6.43 billion stolen as reported by Elliptic — has been frozen or seized, while roughly $3.24 billion remains in addresses linked to the theft, mostly in bitcoin and ether.

The firm said only a negligible amount of stolen funds appeared to have been cashed out, with most of the activity involving transfers or conversions between cryptocurrencies rather than exchanges into spendable funds.

Elliptic said the laundering has moved slower than after the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, when North Korean hackers moved all the stolen ether within 10 days. It expects the remaining funds to be gradually converted into bitcoin and potentially cashed out through over-the-counter brokers and exchanges over several months.

Binanceaddedit has covered about 95% of the affected amount, with the remaining 5% consisting of less liquid tokens that take longer to source. The exchange said it was working with industry partners to acquire the remaining assets.

title: Lovable CEO says AI is collapsing barriers to starting a business
content:
AI is making it easier for people to turn an idea into an app, website or even a business — without needing the same level of technical expertise as before.

Lovable CEO Anton Osika joins CNBC's Arjun Kharpal to explain how AI-powered software development is changing entrepreneurship, product development and the role of developers. He discusses how Lovable has evolved from a platform for building apps and websites with plain-English prompts into a broader tool for helping entrepreneurs build, run and grow their businesses.

They also discuss AI agents, the future of work, competition from the biggest AI labs, regulation and whether Europe can produce the next generation of global AI companies.

title: OpenAI hires former U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for national security role
content:
OpenAIhas hired former U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll as senior counselor for national security modernization, a newly created roleat the company.

Driscoll will focus on how artificial intelligence can be used to strengthen U.S. national security and cybersecurity, OpenAI said, while hisupdatedLinkedIn profile also lists his new position.

He will work with OpenAI's senior leadership and external partners, with a particular focus on helping U.S. allies adopt advanced AI responsibly.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the U.S. has "an extraordinary opportunity to work with other countries to spread the adoption of democratic AI," and that Driscoll's appointment would help strengthen American leadership in the technology.

"National security requirements are changing faster than at any time in the past fifty years," Driscoll said. He added that AI could help reduce paperwork, process information and deliver answers more quickly to those working in national security.

The appointment comes after Driscoll stepped down as Army secretary earlier this year after months ofreportedtensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

An Iraq war veteran, Driscoll pushed efforts to modernize the U.S. military, including expanding access to drone and counter-drone technologies among U.S. allies,accordingto a previous U.S. Army announcement.

Driscoll also met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv in November 2025 to discuss a U.S.-proposed peace plan aimed at ending the war with Russia,accordingto a statement from the Presidential Office of Ukraine.

At OpenAI, Driscoll will work with government officials, industry leaders, academic institutions and allied organizations to advance what the company calls "democratic AI." He will also help internal teams understand the operational needs of national security institutions, building on OpenAI's efforts to strengthen cyber resilience and protect essential services through itsDaybreak program.

title: Christmas 2026 stamps unveiled by Royal Mail
content: Image source,Royal MailImage caption,Two stamps from the Royal Mail's annual Christmas collectionByClaire KeenanPublished6 hours agoRoyal Mail has unveiled its Christmas stamps for this year - featuring scenes from the Nativity.The series of five stamps have been jointly created by graphic designer Gareth Howat and illustrator Rebecca Sutherland.The stamps depict familiar scenes of Mary and Joseph travelling, baby Jesus, an angel, the shepherds and the Three Wise Men.This year's collection marks the 60th anniversary of the first-ever Christmas special stamp.Sutherland said it was an "absolute honour" to be given the opportunity to illustrate the Christmas stamps for the Royal Mail.She said she has loved stamps since she was a child and had even collected them. "Being asked to create a set myself feels incredibly special," she added.The Christmas stamps from recent years have featured snowy scenes of UK cathedrals, or lyrics from famous carols - although 2025 also showed scenes from the Nativity.The first Christmas stamp collection came out in December 1966 after a children's art competition was announced by the then-postmaster Tony Benn.David Gold, of Royal Mail, said: "We hope this year's Christmas stamps will add an extra touch of festive magic to the millions of greetings sent to family and friends at home and around the world."Related topicsChristmasMore on this storyPrice of first class stamp rises to Â£1.80Published7 AprilNativity scenes feature on Christmas stampsPublished4 November 2025

title: Apple unsure when more foldable iPhones will be available after selling out
content: Image source,ReutersByKali HaysTechnology reporterPublished1 hour agoThe new head of Apple says the company is working to get its new foldable iPhones available to more people after the$1,999 smartphonequickly sold out when it was released just over a week ago.John Ternus, who in Septembertook over the roleas Apple's chief executive from Tim Cook, said on Monday that he was "thrilled" at the early reaction to the iPhone Duo.While the costly phone, which sells for Â£1,999 in the UK, immediately sold out, some buyers have seen theirscreens crack.The phones are still in high demand and Sabhi Kahn, Apple's new chief operating officer, said the technology giant did not know when more Duos would be available."At this time, it's really hard to predict when supply and demand will be in balance," Kahn said during a call with financial analysts to discuss Apple's latest financial results.Apple executives did not mention during the call any issues with the iPhone Duo. But last week, the company said it would replace any phones that were impacted by an issue that caused a "small number" of the new phones to crack along the inside fold.Nevertheless, Apple said on Monday that over the last year it sold more iPhones globally than it ever has before.During the three months to 26 September, which did not include sales of the iPhone Duo that went on sale toward the end of October, Apple saw iPhone sales rise 17% to $57bn.Apple has boasted throughout the year that iPhone sales have been surging, despite thecompany's warningsthat crucial components for the device, along with Mac computers and iPads, were constrained to the point of weighing down sales.Sales of Mac computers also grew during the quarter by 27%, hitting $10.7bn, another record for Apple.Overall sales at the company rose by 15% for the year, to $479bn.However, sales for both the iPad and Apple's wearable products, including its headphones and Watch fell by 10% and 7%, respectively.Kahn noted during the call that most Apple devices are still seeing supply constraints driven in part by difficulty in getting enough microprocessors with "advanced nodes."Those components are essentially computer chip technology that allows Apple's devices to operate more quickly, most of which Apple has manufactured through TSMC, which is based in Taiwan.Khan said that such supply constraints are expected to continue into next year, particularly impacting iPads and Macs. The situation has been made worse by what the company has repeatedly insisted is "unexpected demand" for its products.Ternus noted, too, that Apple is still seeing "unprecedented" cost increases for memory, or the ability of Apple devices to store data like apps, photos, and text messages.Much of that memory storage runs through data centres which have seen a huge boom in demand for space as artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots and platforms, including those developed by OpenAI and Anthropic, have become popular.As demand for memory has grown, storage prices have gone up for tech companies like Apple.Cook had earlier this year referred to the sudden increase in data centre costs that Apple was seeing as a "thousand year flood."It has led to the company raising prices on essentially all of its hardware products by around 20%.Related topicsAppleiPhonesTim CookComputersArtificial intelligence

title: Trump focuses on Reflecting Pool in final public speech before midterms
content:
PresidentDonald Trumpbegan his final scheduled in-person speech before Tuesday'sElection Daywith a lengthy disquisition about his efforts to renovate the Lincoln MemorialReflecting Pooland other sites inWashington.

"Today I'm thrilled to announce the official opening of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool," Trump said Monday afternoon in front of the water feature, which was fenced off for months amid a problem-plagued renovation the president had ordered.

The speech, which lasted nearly an hour, was expected to serve as Trump's "closing argument" on the midterms before millions of voters head to the polls to determine which party will control the House and Senate in the next Congress.

But Trump kicked off his remarks with more than 20 minutes of commentary that focused largely on the Reflecting Pool, along with his administration's work on refurbishing other Washington-area monuments and cracking down on crime in the nation's capital.

"The pool is now better and more beautiful than it's ever been before, and we're very proud of it," Trump said, before repeating unfounded claims that vandals were responsible for damaging the pool and delaying repairs.

U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro told acourt July 31that the damage was caused by a contractor's botched installation. Trump lashed out at Pirro over the admission and has continued to claim vandals were to blame.

Trump's first explicit reference to the midterms came around the 23-minute mark.

"As you know, this is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm, I believe, in our lifetime," Trump said.

"The Democrat Party has nominated the most extreme and dangerous slate of candidates in American history," he said.

He touted his administration's record and lashed out at some Democratic candidates by name, including Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. He also repeated his controversial claim that if Republicans win, "everybody is going to get $5,000."

"We have to keep our Congress strong, free," Trump said. "America is ready to go. They're ready to vote. I hope they're ready to do the right thing."

But Trump, as he has done in other recent remarks, seemed to acknowledge that Democrats had an advantage — at least when looking to historical trends that show the president's party tends to underperform in midterm elections.

"For some reason, the sitting president doesn't win the midterms. But we gave this a very strong shot," he said.

Later in the speech, Trump continued discussing the pool, as well as his push to erect a massive triumphal arch in Washington and his plans to build a promenade along the Potomac River.

He also said the government planned to build a "National Garden of American Heroes," comprising "250 to 500 great American heroes in statue form." And he talked about ongoing efforts to renovate a public golf course in Washington that is subject to legal challenges.

title: Crude oil prices sell off more than 7% on Iran peace talk hopes ahead of U.S. midterms
content:
Crude oil prices fell sharply Monday as the presidents of the U.S. and Iran signal they are open to a diplomatic solution to the conflict that has disrupted energy markets for eight months.

Brent crudefutures, the international benchmark, fell 7.4% to $105 a barrel as of 2:48 p.m. ET. U.S.West Texas Intermediatedeclined 7.3% to settle at $96.46 per barrel.

President Donald Trump told reporters Monday that Iran wants to "make a deal and that could happen." U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubiosaidover the weekendthat Trump prefers not to use military force against Iran and would like to resolve the conflict diplomatically.

Trump has previously said that he will not attack Iran before the U.S. midterms. But the oil market had priced in the risk of a major military escalation after the elections, gaining more than 10% in October.

The president "hasn't made a decision," Rubio told reporters.

"What the president expresses to you is incredible confidence that if we needed to do something militarily, we would have the ability to do it," the secretary of State said. "But we would prefer to do it peacefully."

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran is seeking to resolve problems through dialogue, according to state-ownedIslamic Republic News Agency. Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei has granted the government certain authorities to do this, Pezeshkian said.

Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said an agreement with the U.S. is possible if Washington "demonstrates goodwill" and is "truly seeking a peaceful solution," according to IRNA.

Araghchi said mediators are discussing the proposal Iran made during the United Nations General Assembly in September. Tehran expects the U.S. to lift sanctions, reduce its military presence in the region to previous levels and lift the blockade, the foreign minister said.

But Khamenei on Saturday called for Tehran's armed forces to meet "any level or type of threat" with "an immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response."

Reports about diplomatic efforts will have a big impact on crude oil prices because much of the market's recent gains were risk premium in anticipation of a possible escalation, according to Ryan McKay, director of commodity strategy at TD Securities.

"With that said, so long as there is no concrete conclusion to the war, and tanker and Houthi attacks remain prevalent, we do not anticipate a complete erosion of the risk premium via diplomacy headlines alone," McKay said.

— CNBC's Lim Hui Jie contributed to this report.

title: Apple earnings live updates: New CEO John Ternus faces first Wall Street test
content:
Applereports fiscal fourth-quarter earnings after the bell on Monday, with new CEOJohn Ternusexpected to address Wall Street in a meaningful way for the first time.

Here's what analysts are expecting, according to LSEG.

Revenue is expected to increase 11% from $102.5 billion a year earlier. Analysts project $56.59 billion in iPhone sales for the quarter.

Wall Street is closely watching iPhone revenue because the report will include eight days of new iPhone 18 Pro sales. But Apple's new flagship device, the iPhone Duo, didn't hit store shelves until the quarter was over, and Apple didn't announce a new entry-level iPhone 18.

Apple also raised prices on iPhones by $100, which may have hurt demand in the quarter.

Monday's earnings call, set to start at 5 p.m. ET, will be the first with Ternus at the helm. Investors want to hear from him about the company's plans in China after its AI software got approved, as well as the slew of recent product launches and how the company continues to grapple with global shortages of memory and flash storage.

While Monday's earnings report won't include sales from the iPhone Duo, execs may still be pressed on the device's launch in October.

There hasn't been much supply of the folding iPhone, with first-day preorders quickly slipping into estimated ship dates in 2027.

But there are also a number of reports that theDuo can crackunder normal use, which is a tough hit to Apple's brand under Ternus. Apple acknowledged the issues last month and said they affected a "small number" of devices.

Analysts at Barclays wrote in an earnings preview over the weekend that they "remain cautious on the stock given iPhone uncertainties this cycle, limited monetization of AI, and renewed fears on the App Store."

The firm has an underweight rating on the shares, and said the "pricing benefits AAPL has been enjoying from the memory backdrop due to its scale and preferential pricing are fading."

Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan said on Friday that his team had a "conservative outlook" on earnings because of gross margin concerns and price increases.

The analyst pointed out that Apple's gross margins in the September quarter will be boosted by a positive impact from tariff refunds, and that margins could drop in the coming quarters.

Apple reported a gross margin of 49.3% in its June quarter, but warned that it would be between 47.5% and 48% in the September period.

"Investor focus will likely be on component cost inflation, durability of gross margin and services revenue growth," Mohan wrote in the note.

Bank of America maintains a Buy rating on the stock and a price target of $370.

Apple is competing in a smartphone and PC market that has "never been worse," IDC's Ryan Reith told CNBC.

Consumer electronics companies everywhere are grappling with surging prices for computer parts, including memory and flash storage that's used in every smartphone and laptop.

Intelon Friday had its worst day on the stock market since the 1970s, dropping 29%, after the company cited PC softness for adisappointing forecast.

Many companies have responded to component shortages by raising prices or reducing specifications for current devices. Consumers are holding onto their old computers for far longer, driving sales down.

IDC says the smartphone market is set to dropnearly 17%this year based on shipments. PCs couldbe down 11%.

Apple isn't immune. The company raised prices on almost all of its products since executives warned over the summer that the market was in a "thousand year flood."

Apple's new $2,000 foldable phone won't have any sales for the quarter, which ended last month. While Apple and Ternus announced new iPhones on Sept. 9, the foldable Duo didn't go on sale until a month later, on Oct 23.

Some analysts have theorized that Apple's most committed fans may have been waiting to see the Duo come out before buying it.

There will be a few weeks of sales from the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, which went on sale on Sept. 18.

Apple investors and customers are still getting to know Ternus, but since he took over forTim Cookon Sept. 1, the new CEO has embraced his new role as the face of the iPhone company.

Ternus' first major appearance came nine days into his tenure, when he unveiled the iPhone Duo at Apple's headquarters. A week later, he was walking the red carpet at the Emmys. He then flew to New York, where he opened the doors at an Apple store to commemorate the new iPhone Pro going on sale. He also went to Austin, Texas, this month to kick off sales of the iPhone Duo, and appeared at an elementary school and an F1 race while on the trip.

And he's had a busy media schedule, including an appearance on the cover of Time magazine.

Last week, Ternus continued a new style of Apple product introduction in unveiling the first MacBook with a touchscreen using a format he first tried out in the spring. That's when Apple launched its low-cost MacBook Neo. Ternus addressed a crowd of media and analysts, giving a five minute speech interspersed with a few short videos.

Investors will get their first in-depth look at Ternus on Monday. He's been on the past few calls, but hasn't given extended remarks, and largely deferred to Cook when asked questions.

Heading into its earnings report, Apple has emerged as the preferred megacap tech stock on Wall Street. The shares are up 27% this year as of Friday's close, by far outpacing Apple's leading peers.

It's also the last among the group (other than Nvidia, which reports next month) to issue quarterly earnings. Investors weren't kind to the hyperscalers over the past two weeks, scrutinizing their hefty expenses and dwindling cash flows.

Apple is in a much different category as the iPhone maker has avoided running up huge capital expenditures bills, taking a more measured approach to its AI investing.

title: Trump Account holders to receive SpaceX stock from Gwynne Shotwell in December
content:
EligibleTrump Accountholders will begin receiving donated shares ofSpaceXstock next month, according to anX poston Friday.

"Robert and I are thrilled that our gift of over 2 million shares of SpaceX stock will be distributed to children's Trump accounts in December!" President and COOGwynne Shotwellwrote in the post.

The giftfrom Shotwell and her husband will provide a share apiece to around 2 million Trump Accounts holders ages 11 to 17 who live in ZIP codes with median family incomes of $57,000 or less, or in ZIP codes with too few residents for a median family income to be reported by the U.S. Census Bureau. These families should receive a notice by Monday, Shotwell wrote on X.

"In a few weeks, an additional gift will be finalized for eligible 11 to 17-year-old children in military families serving overseas, children in foster care, and more children whose MFI is $90,000 or less living in counties near our home in the great state of Texas," she also wrote.

Parents or guardians cancheck eligibilityfor the donation through Invest America, a nonprofit advocacy group, and track account activity with theTrump Accounts app.

Trump Accounts, also known as 530A accounts, are open to any U.S. child under 18 with a Social Security number.

Children born from 2025 through 2028 may also receive a one-time$1,000 depositfrom the U.S. Department of the Treasury.

Other funds may also be available, depending on certain criteria. In a separate funding announcement in October, Elon Muskwrote in an X postthat he plans togive every kid in Americaa share ofSpaceXsometime in 2027, which may also come viaTrump Accounts.

The U.S. Department of the Treasuryrolled outtemporary regulationsat the end of September that allow Trump Accounts to hold donated individual stocks, a change from previous guidelines that only allowed diversified, low-costindex funds.

The move to permit stock donations could pave the way for more large-scale philanthropic gifts, Internal Revenue Service CEO Frank Bisignano told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Oct. 8.

On Oct. 29, Bisignanoannouncedhis own donation toTrump Accountsfor eligible children ages 2 to 8 living in 11234, Bisignano's hometown ZIP code, according to The Bisignano Family Fund.

title: S&P 500 pulls back as tech stock losses outweigh cooler oil prices ahead of midterms: Live updates
content:
The S&P 500 edged down on the day, curtailing earlier gains, as investors assessed cooling oil prices and braced for the upcoming midterm elections

TheS&P 500traded 0.2% lower, while theNasdaq Compositefell 0.6%. TheDow Jones Industrial Averageadded 310 points, or 0.6%.

At its high, the S&P 500 was up 1.1%, but the index curtailed its gains as the tech sector pulled back further.

Meanwhile,Brent crudetumbled nearly 8% to around $104 per barrel. U.S.West Texas Intermediate futuresalso pulled back more than 7% to roughly $96.

Oil prices fell amid hopes that the U.S. and Iran may resume peace talks, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio saying over the weekend that PresidentDonald Trump"hasn't made a decision" to attack Iran and that Washington would prefer to resolve the conflict "peacefully." Iranian state media also reported that the country's foreign minister said an agreement with is possible if the U.S. "demonstrates goodwill."

Investors moved into key cyclical sectors. Consumer discretionary stocks led the way, with the group gaining 3%, while financials and industrials added more than 1%. Materials advanced 2%.

Technology, however, came under pressure yet again.Marvell Technologyshares dropped about 12%, whileLumentumshed 18% after the companies announced that Marvell is buying Lumentum in a$115 billion deal.Oracleshares also declined 8% after the company said itplans to sell $10 billion in common stockas well as $10 billion in bonds to finance its AI buildout.

The moves come after the major U.S. stock benchmarks suffered a losing week, bogged down byselling pressure in techas investors continued to scrutinize names related to the AI buildout.

"The stock market's longer-term bullish narrative may have taken some hits in recent weeks, but it's still intact," said Chris Larkin, managing director of trading and investing at E-Trade. "The challenge has been short-term momentum — stringing together more than a few days without being disrupted by surging oil prices, concerns about AI spending, inflation, or geopolitics."

Last week, the tech-heavy Nasdaq and the S&P 500 logged a losing October amid AI spending concerns, with the Nasdaq suffering its worst losses since March 2025. The Dow, however, rose almost 2% as investors rotated into defensive areas like healthcare.

"The market has more potential 'volatility triggers' to face — including this week's midterms and jobs data — but its ability to bend but not break under pressure has been a positive sign," Larkin added.

The U.S. midterm elections will be held on Tuesday, when Democrats are expected to take control of the House of Representatives, while Senate control remains uncertain.

In addition to the closely watched monthly jobs report, a fresh round of earnings releases is also due this week. "Magnificent Seven" memberAppleis scheduled to report after the bell on Monday.McDonald'sandQualcommare slated to report later in the week.

Correction: An earlier version of this story misstated the move in oil prices in the session.

Stephens upgradedOracleto overweight from equal weight on Monday.

"We believe the market needs to give Oracle more credit for the execution on delivering compute that continues to happen," wrote Analyst Brett Huff, who noted the company delivered about 850 MW in the first quarter across 38 projects in 11 countries.

Huff added it sees Oracle may reach "double-digit" multi-year growth in applications, higher than what Wall Street's 10% growth estimate.

The firm gave Oracle a $213 price target, implying a roughly 63% upside from Friday's close.

Check out some of the companies making the biggest moves midday:

Loop Capital is pulling down its rating on social media siteRedditto a hold from a buy. The investment bank has a price target of $100 on the stock.

The downgrade is due to pressures on referral traffic as AI supplants traditional internet searching at the dominant search engineGoogle. The bank also has concerns about mandatory log-ins for the site, monetization trends, and the prospects for Google's licensing deal with Reddit.

"It seems increasingly likely that Google does not renew its licensing agreement expiring early 2027," Rob Sanderson at Loop Capital wrote.

Google reported a significant dent in its core advertising revenues last week, leading to its largest single-day stock decline ever on Thursday.

Construction spending in September fell at its fastest monthly level since the Covid pandemic, weighed by a sharp drop in residential activity.

The Commerce Department reported Monday that the metric slipped 1.9% for the month, posting the biggest monthly decline since April 2020. On a year-over-year basis, construction spending was off 2.7%.

Residential spending was off 5.5%, more than offsetting a 0.6% increase in nonresidential outlays. Economists surveyed by Dow Jones had been looking for an increase of 0.4%. Private construction spending fell 2.4%, while public construction expenditures were off 0.1%.

Deutsche Bank has shifted back to an overweight rating on the tech sector after downgrading it to neutral earlier this month amid ongoing volatility.

The sector's "relative performance is now at the bottom of its long-run trend channel, a level from which it has V-turned up 5 times in the last 2 1/2 years," analyst Parag Thatte said in a Friday note to clients.

The Nasdaq-100 slid roughly 8% since Deutsche Bank issued its downgrade to a neutral rating on Oct. 9. On Friday alone, the index dropped by about 3.5%. Now, analysts at the bank see the trend reversing, with potentially positive effects for the broader market.

"The risk-reward now favors going overweight again. On average, these rotations into Tech have seen it rise 32%, outperforming the rest of the S&P 500 by 30pp. We note that S&P 500 performance in previous rotations into Tech has been very strong (up 16% over 3 months on average)," Thatte said.

U.S. factory activity accelerated in October as production ramped up, order backlogs declined and inventories swelled, the Institute for Supply Management reported Monday.

The ISM manufacturing index increased to 55.5, a 1-point jump from September that was better than the 54.5 consensus estimate from Dow Jones. The index measures the percentage of companies reporting growth.

Within the survey, the prices index slipped to 75.2, down 2.7 points, while inventories rose 2.8 points to 51.4 — out of contraction territory — and production increased to 59.0, up 2.3 points. Order backlogs declined 1.8 points to 54.6 and the employment index came in at 52.3, down just 0.3 points.

Amazon's spending spree on artificial intelligence will net big results for the hyperscaler, according to PhillipCapital. The firm upgraded the stock to buy on Monday and raised its price target to $330, which implies 37% upside ahead.

Amazon sold off on Thursday after holding its full-year guidance oncapital expenditures at $220 billionand saying it will spend meaningfully more next year. It also reported negative free cash flow, amounting to $42.2 billion in outflows.

However, PhillipCapital believes Amazon is well positioned in artificial intelligence because it is model-agnostic and has a full stack of capabilities, analyst Helena Wang said in a note to clients.

"Aggressive CapEx creates FCF pressure, but strong demand visibility supports sustained infrastructure investment," she wrote. "We believe these investments will benefit AMZN over the long term, strengthen its market leadership and create significant barriers to entry for potential competitors."

The three leading U.S. indexes traded higher on Monday morning.

The S&P 500 rose 0.5% just after 9:30 a.m. ET, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 0.7%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average moved up 405 points, or 0.8%.

HyperscalerOracleoffered $10 billion worth ofcommon stockon Monday amid the ongoing AI buildout, which is facing capital availabilityconcerns. The book runners for the issuance include Wells Fargo, Citigroup and BNP Paribas, among several other banks.

Shares of Oracle were down more than 2.5% in premarket trading.

Oil prices extended earlier declines following reports that Iran's supreme leader granted some authority to the government to hold peace talks.Brent crudetumbled 6.1% to $106.50 per barrel. U.S.West Texas Intermediate futuresalso pulled back more than 6% to $97.70.

Goldman Sachs upgradedBritish American Tobaccoto buy from neutral.

"For investors, we see a differentiated opportunity set: BAT offers the clearest growth inflection, while Imperial combines resilient cash generation with compelling value and capital returns.," wrote analyst Aron Adamski.

The firm sees pouches, vapor and heated tobacco as "growth vectors" and expects tighter regulation on illicit vapor will help regulated brands. British American Tobacco is well positioned to lead in transitioning the industry to smokeless nicotine, the bank added.

Goldman Sachs also raised its 12-month price target for British American Tobacco to 5,600 pence, implying a 22% upside.

Marvell Technologyis buying optical-components makerLumentumin adeal valued at $115 billion, creating a major new force in AI connectivity.

"AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity,"said Matt Murphy, Marvell's chairman and CEO. "By bringing together two leaders with highly complementary technologies, we intend to help shape the next era of AI connectivity and create exceptional s

title: DOJ asks Supreme Court to block California counting disputed mail-in ballots
content:
The Trump administration on Monday asked theSupreme Courtto temporarily blockCaliforniafrom counting mail-in ballots of about 20,000 voters whom the Department of Justice suggests may not beU.S. citizens.

TheDOJ's petition to the Supreme Court came three days after the 9th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals rejected the department's bid to overturn a federal district court judge's ruling that allowed the ballots to be counted.

The petition comes a day beforeElection Day. The Supreme Court could act on the petition at any time, but there is no deadline.

The midterm elections will determine which parties hold majorities in both chambers of Congress.

"In this case, this Office has been informed that the United States has identified more than 20,000 individuals who appear to be registered to vote in California based on publicly available information at the time that information was received, but who, in the United States' view, are likely not U.S. citizens," Solicitor General D. John Sauer said in application to the Supreme Court on Monday.

Sauer said "the United States is likely to succeed on the merits of its appeal" of the lower court ruling denying the DOJ's request.

"The district court concluded that the United States lacks Article III standing to bring this suit, but the United States suffers a judicially cognizable 'injury to its sovereignty' from the 'violation of its laws,'" Sauer said in the petition. "Once California commingles the challenged ballots with lawful ones, there is no way to get the challenged ballots back."

The DOJ sued California on Oct. 15 in U.S. District Court in Los Angeles. The complaint sought to prevent state election officials from tabulating mail-in ballots "from likely non-citizens in the upcoming federal election until the voter's citizenship status can be determined."

The DOJ previously gave Los Angeles County officials a thumb drive containing names of voters the department suggested could be noncitizens, who by law are barred from voting in federal elections.

Last Wednesday, Judge David Carter denied the DOJ's request that he order California officials to set aside mail ballots from alleged noncitizens namedon a list prepared by the Department of Homeland Security, and not count their votes until their citizenship is confirmed.

"This case is about the right of every American citizen to vote in a free and fair election," Carter said in his ruling.

"Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch," Carter wrote.

"In bringing this lawsuit, the Executive would have this Court believe that it reigns as a sole sovereign. But California and its people are sovereign, too."

The DOJ then appealed that ruling to the 9th Circuit. A three-judge panel on that court denied the appeal in a 2-1 ruling on Friday

"There is a material risk that granting the United States its requested relief would result in disenfranchisement," said the ruling by the majority, Circuit Judges Mark Bennett and Gabriel Sanchez. Bennett was appointed by PresidentDonald Trump, and Sanchez was appointed by former PresidentJoe Biden.

On Sunday, a federal judge dismissed a DOJ lawsuit that sought to block Alaska election officials from immediately certifying the result of the U.S. Senate election there if incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses that race by a margin that could be attributable to voter confusion about another candidate with his name.

The DOJ is appealing that ruling.

title: Ryanair CEO warns fares could rise by up to 20% in 2027 as fuel bill jumps by $2.2 billion
content:
RyanairCEO Michael O'Leary told CNBC Monday that European airfares are set to rise "significantly," growing by as much as 20% next year as fuel hedges expire.

The budget air carrier's profit fell 15% to 2.15 billion euros ($2.3 billion) in the first fiscal half of the year, as the price of its 20% unhedged jet fuel doubled.

"So we're facing 2027 where we have much higher oil prices... I think they're going to get passed on in significantly higher airfares," O'Leary told CNBC'sSteve Sedgwickon Monday.

"The market customers have been insulated for the last 12 months... but those hedges are rolling off. There's still no resolution in the Middle East. Jet oil today is $170 a barrel. I mean, this is a very significant cost cliff we're all facing next year. I believe you're going to see airfares rise next year across Europe by 10%, maybe even 20%," O'Leary added.

Ryanair said it doesn't expect an increase in short-haul airfares to fully offset an estimated 2-billion-euro increase in fuel charges next year. It is therefore launching a cost review, which will include lowering crew rations, a potential temporary pay freeze and the use of AI to drive further efficiencies.

Ryanair's Irish-listed shares initially edged higher in early Monday trading before paring gains to trade below the flatline. The stock has fallen over 22% this year.

The airline said in September it would cut its full-year traffic target from 216 million passengers to 214 million passengers in a bid to reduce its exposure to unhedged fuel during the winter. It's now expecting winter traffic between November and March to remain broadly flat year-on-year.

"I think you're seeing even this winter, all of the airlines across Europe, even Ryanair, for the first time in many years, we cut our winter capacity," O'Leary said. We'll only be flat this winter over the prior year, because it makes no sense for us to be growing capacity if we're buying unhedged oil at $170 a barrel."

Ryanair hedged 80% of its jet fuel at $67 per barrel for the year, which it said gave it an advantage over its competitors as its earnings remained insulated from volatile oil prices. The carrier added that it has hedged at least 25% of its 2028 jet fuel prices at $95 per barrel.

The share price reaction on Monday says more about investors' expectations than the numbers alone, according to Adam Vetesse, market analyst at eToro.

"Investors appear to have already priced in the hit from unhedged fuel and softer summer fares, leaving room for relief that the quarter landed exactly where consensus had predicted," Vetesse said.

"Near-term earnings remain hostage to oil prices and close-in bookings, but the market's early bounce suggests investors are willing to give Ryanair the benefit of the doubt that its cost advantage will matter more than the fuel spike once the dust settles," he added.

Ryanair also noted in Monday's announcement that it held 2.6 billion euros in cash as of 30 September, even after repaying 1.3 billion euros in debt.

"You know we've paid off all of our debt this year, so we have effectively zero debt. We have 650 aircraft on the balance sheet. We're significantly cash positive," O'Leary told CNBC, adding that the challenge facing all airlines is the volatility in oil prices, lack of hedging, and higher financing costs.

"So you see, some of our competitors are doing sale and leasebacks to generate cash. They're just mortgaging their futures; they're Ponzi schemes."

title: South Korea targets 'world's highest performance' sovereign AI model in record new budget
content:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung unveiled the country's largest ever budget on Monday, pledging to "boldly invest in AI and future growth engines."

Speaking to the National Assemblyon Monday, Lee said total spending for 2027 would rise 12.8% to 820.9 trillion won ($610.14 billion), including 21.3 trillion won for semiconductors, physical AI and AI data centers — nearly double the 2026 level.

A separate 4.7 trillion won will go toward developing a sovereign AI model with what Lee described as the "world's highest performance."

The government also plans to invest heavily into talent, including training 2,000 specialists to "lead semiconductor design and the regional semiconductor industry," while expanding AI education for students, job seekers and existing workers.

South Koreahas set upuniversity "contract departments," where students can enroll in company-linked degrees that offer pathways to jobs at firms like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix before graduation.

Companies help design courses, provide financial support and recruit qualifying graduates.

The record spending plan comes as theInternational Monetary Fundforecasts South Korea's economy will grow 3.3% in 2026, its fastest pace since the post pandemic rebound in 2021.

Lee said the higher spending would result in "virtually no net increase in government debt," with newly issued bonds used to repay existing debt.

The budget also increases spending on defense and social security spending for the youth. Defense expenditure is set to rise 8.2% to 73.3 trillion won.

"We will rapidly transform into a smart, elite, and powerful military by establishing a hybrid manned and unmanned system based on AI, robots, and drones," Lee said.

South Korea's strong economic growth has been driven largely by semiconductor exports as global demand for computing power rises with the AI boom.

Exports surged 93.7% from a year earlier to a record $115.3 billion in October, according to data released Sunday by the Korea Customs Service.

Shipments totaled $930 billion in the first 10 months of 2026, surpassing the $900 billion mark for the first time.

The country posted a $42.5 billion trade surplus in October, with imports rising 36% year on year to $72.8 billion.

Lee said South Korea was within reach of $1 trillion in annual exports, citing strong performance in key industries including semiconductors.

title: Sam Altman makes surprise South Korea visit as OpenAI builds on chip partnerships
content:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman made an unannounced visit to South Korea over the weekend, meeting with Samsung executives and reportedly holding talks with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, building on existing partnerships with the country's leading chipmakers.

SamsungsaidSaturday that Altman met with around 50 executives from its affiliates spanning electronics, finance and biotechnology in Yongin, south of Seoul.

The discussions covered AI developments, potential business opportunities and the technology's impact on corporate decision-making and operations, Samsung said.

Altman also met with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won over lunch Saturday, with senior executives from SK Hynix and SK Telecom in attendance,accordingto South Korean media reports.

The two sides may have discussed cooperation on AI chips and data centers, including existing plans for high-bandwidth memory supplies and AI data center development, according to local media reports. The participants didn't provide details of the discussions.

SK Hynix told CNBC it was unable to confirm the reported meeting.

Altman also visited South Korea in October 2025, when hemetwith President Lee Jae Myung, Samsung Electronics Executive Chairman Jay Y. Lee and SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, and announced partnerships with Samsung and SK Group as part of OpenAI's Stargate initiative.

OpenAI's Stargate initiative aims to expand AI infrastructure globally, with South Korea playing a role through partnerships focused on advanced memory chip supplies and AI data center development.

Under the agreements, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix outlined plans to ramp up production of advanced memory chips, while OpenAI and its South Korean partners agreed to explore developing AI data centers in the country.

OpenAIcitedSouth Korea's ranking among global leaders in AI readiness and significant public-private funding to strengthen competitiveness as reasons for expanding its presence in the country.

Altman's latest visit also follows a July meeting with Samsung Electronics Executive Chairman Jay Y. Lee at OpenAI's headquarters in San Francisco, according to Samsung.

Altman left South Korea on Saturday, according to local media reports.

title: Rubio says Trump wants to end Iran war 'peacefully' even as both sides prepare for strikes
content:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Donald Trump would like to resolve the Iranian war "diplomatically," and prefers not to use military force.

Speaking over the weekend, Rubio told reporters that "He [Trump] hasn't made a decision...what the president expresses to you is incredible confidence that if we needed to do something militarily, we would have the ability to do it, and we really we have everything we need to be successful. But we would prefer to do it peacefully."

The remarks come as reports suggest both sides are gearing up for additional military strikes after the midterm elections.

On Saturday, Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei called for Tehran's armed forces to meet "any level or type of threat" with "an immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response."

He also ordered that its military database be updated so that "all kinds of physical and non-physical assets of the U.S.-Zionist enemy are brought within the reach of the Armed Forces," referring to U.S. and Israeli forces.

Washington has not explicitly stated it plans to resume attacks on Iran, butreports from The Wall Street Journaland The New York Times indicate the U.S. is preparing forpossible renewed military actionsafter the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

On Sunday, Trump told theRight Side Broadcasting Network."We've had such a victory, and we'll put it away very soon, one way or the other."

"Either they'll make a deal, or we'll just end it," he added.

On Sunday, Iran's foreign ministry designated the U.K.'s Military Intelligence Services as a "hostile group" and accused the Royal Navy and Air Force of supporting "terrorist organizations."In a Telegram post, the ministry said that the move was a response to what it called London's "malicious" actions, including the designation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a "terrorist organization."

Tehran has separately accused the U.K. of participating in the U.S.-Iran war by allowing American forces access to British military and logistical bases.

The U.K. had allowed U.S. forces to use RAF Fairford and Diego Garcia for what were described as "defensive" strikes on Iran,according to the BBC.
