title: Stellantis reports $4.5 billion cash drain as massive turnaround plan continues
content:
European car giantStellantisreported a 4 billion euro ($4.5 billion) cash shortfall in the third quarter as it ploughed ahead with its $70 billion turnaround strategy to restore profitability.

Third-quarter revenuesrose 1% to 37.6 billion euros from a year ago, the Chrysler and Jeep owner said on Wednesday, while adjusted operating income rose 184% to 256 million euros from 90 million euros a year earlier.

The company also reported that negative industrial free cash flow improved to 4 billion euros, up from 4.3 billion the year prior. Stellantis shares were up 3.6% shortly after the European market opened, but have declined 62% since the beginning of the year.

The announcement came as the transatlantic company continues to implement a60 billion euro ($66.7 billion) turnaround strategyafter years of sales declines, especially in North America. Stellantis reaffirmed that it expects positive industrial free cash flow in 2027

"During the quarter, we continued to make progress in the early execution of our FaSTLAne 2030 plan, launching new products, accelerating partnerships as planned, and delivering meaningful improvements in manufacturing and quality," Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa said in the report.

In May, Filosa laid out a five-year plan to achieve positive free cash flow by 2027.

This includes investing 36 billion euros in its portfolio of automotive brands, with 60% of the cash to go towards its struggling North America sector. It also plans to introduce new vehicles, refresh models, and incorporate new technologies in its products.

European carmakers, including Stellantis, have been struggling in China as domestic brands like Xiaomi, BYD and Geely gain ground and intensify competition.

Just this week, German luxury carmaker Porsche said it wouldreduce its exposure to Chinaas car sales decline in the region. Meanwhile,Mercedes-Benzsaid its third-quarter car sales slumped due to a "challenging market environment," in the country.

Earlier this month,Filosa told CNBCthat European regulators need to do more to incentivize carmakers to manufacture vehicles in the region to fend off Chinese rivals.

Filosa called for regulation that "incentivizes, rewards, and protects the ones that are able to demonstrate that they design cars, engineer cars."

- CNBC's Michael Wayland contributed to this report.

title: Musk's PAC lawyer runs in Texas House district that is home to billionaire's business interests
content:
Two years ago,Chris Goberwas leadingElon Musk's political operation. Now, the former director and top lawyer forMusk's America PACwants a seat in Congress representing Texas' 10th District, which is home to part of the Tesla and SpaceX CEO's growing business empire.

With less than a week until Election Day, Gober isn't exactly touting his connection to the world's richest person, as he tries to secure a Republican victory in an open seat considered a safe GOP win.

The 10th District is home tothe Terafab, a sprawling artificial intelligence chip factory being built by Musk's companiesTeslaandSpaceX. The district also cuts through Pflugerville, which houses offices for Musk's tunneling venture, The Boring Co.

While Gober is not talking about his work for Musk as a key pillar of his campaign, his Democratic opponent Caitlin Rourk scathingly highlighted it in a newad.

"Elon Musk already had MAGA extremist Chris Gober as his lawyer. Now he wants him in Congress," a voice on the ad says. "It's clear who Chris Gober would serve in Congress, and it's not us."

Gober's campaign websitetouts an endorsementfrom PresidentDonald Trump, and in the"key issues"section, the candidate says he will be "standing strong for President Trump and delivering his America First Agenda" if elected.

But neither Musk's name nor that of America PAC appeared on the campaign's site as of Tuesday.

Gober, in an email from campaign manager Zach Gregory, told CNBC, "My work with America PAC has been widely reported and is no secret."

"I've discussed it throughout this campaign as one of the many examples of taking on the toughest fights at the highest levels," he said.

Gober said Musk and America PAC are not mentioned on his campaign site because it was updated in the final weeks of the election "to focus on the priorities I'm running to deliver for the people of Texas's 10th Congressional District."

SpaceX's political action committee has donated $10,000 to Gober's campaign this election cycle, according to Federal Election Commission filings.Axiosfirst reported the filing Monday.

SpaceX hasexpandedaggressively into AI in 2026.

The segment has become the company's largest business unit, with third-quarter revenue surging ninefold to $7.56 billion from $813 million a year earlier, according to its Oct. 20earnings update.

Gober's campaign website deleted a section that had been titled "Ensuring America's AI Dominance," Axios reported in its article Monday, amidopposition to data centersused for AI.

Gober told CNBC the section's removal does not reflect a shift in his position.

"I believe Texas should lead the country in AI and innovation, and that growth has to work for the communities that make it possible," he said. "That means protecting our water and power supply, building the infrastructure to support it, and making sure rural communities share in the benefits."

Rourk criticized Gober's coziness with the AI industry and Musk, saying "There's just so much to his background that is really concerning."

"I think he's trying to bury his head in the sand, and just kind of wait until Election Day, hope that people won't notice," Rourk, a U.S. Army veteran and formerDell Technologiesemployee, told CNBC.

"If he wins a seat in Congress, he can sit there for the next 10, 20, 30 years where he is going to vote to tether taxpayer dollars in defense to SpaceX, in transportation to Tesla and vote against anything like a subpoena of Elon Musk," she said, alluding tobipartisan worriesover SpaceX's dealings in Ukraine and Democrats' calls to investigate Musk over his Department of Government Efficiency work slashing the federal workforce.

Musk did not respond to an email seeking comment.

Attacks over AI go both ways in the campaigns. Gober's campaignin a YouTube adand in an email to CNBC claimed Rourk makes a majority of her household income from investments in data centers.

Rourk called that accusation laughable.

She said she owns some Dell stock she acquired through employee equity grants when she worked there from 2021 to 2025. Rourk said she would sell those shares, which are not a source of household income for her, if she is elected to Congress.

If elected, she said her focus would include "ending forever wars including President Trump's reckless war in Iran," and on "fighting special interests."

Asked about his opponent's accusation that he would work for Musk more than the people of Texas, Gober told CNBC, "I will make decisions based on what is best for my constituents. Period."

"I'm proud of my career and I'm not going to hide from it," he said. "I've worked at the highest levels of politics and public policy, and I intend to turn that experience into an asset for the people of Texas' 10th Congressional District."

Gober's law firm, Lex Politica, is representing Musk and his America PAC in two would-be class actionlawsuitsinAustin federal courtthat alleged Musk and the PAC defrauded people in swing states during the 2024 election by promising a daily $1 million prize for randomly selected people who signed a petition to support the U.S. Constitution and conservative causes.

Gober, during a Nov. 4, 2024 hearing in a Philadelphia courtroom held on the eve of Election Day, revealed that the 18 prizewinners were "not chosen by random, as in a lottery drawing, but that the super PAC instead selects the winners based on who it believes would be effective political spokespeople,"NBC Newsreported at the time.

Lex Politica and other attorneys for Musk and America PAC and lawyers for the plaintiffs on Oct. 15 told the Texas judges overseeing the cases in Austin that they hadagreed to settlethe civil suits.

Terms of the settlement were not revealed, and Musk's PAC had denied any wrongdoing.

Gober told CNBC on Tuesday that he's "proactively working" with the House Ethics Committee to comply with all their rules, and if elected, he will "withdraw from all ongoing representations" since members of Congress are banned from practicing law outside of limited pro bono work.

Whether Musk will be a boon or detriment to Gober's campaign remains to be seen.

Ben Leff, CEO of the survey companyVerasight, told CNBC in an email that his firm found that Musk is "judged by Americans through a partisan lens."

In an Aprilsurveyof 2,000 U.S. adults, Verasight found that 74% of Democrats have a somewhat or very unfavorable view toward Musk, compared to 53% of Independents and 17% of Republicans.

Among Americans who identify as members of Trump's MAGA movement, 85% believe that Musk represents the movement.

"In close races, candidates who are backed by or associated with Musk might face additional challenges in an already weak election cycle for Republicans," Leff said.

title: Meta- and Google-backed Jio Platforms’ shares soar over 21% on trading debut after record IPO
content:
Jio Platforms' shares rose 21.4% on their trading debut Wednesday after a record initial public offering that was lapped up by retail as well as institutional investors.

India's largest telecom and digital services player had offered 270 million shares inthe IPO pricedat 1,119 rupees apiece, raising 302 billion rupees ($3.2 billion) in the country's largest-ever IPO.

The public issue was subscribed more than 22 times, with institutional investors leading the demand, according to data from the BSE. The qualified institutional portion was subscribed 70.55 times, while retail investors subscribed 2.72 times.

The IPO was fully subscribed within 95 minutes of its opening on Oct. 21, Akash Ambani, managing director of Jio Platforms and heir of the Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani, said ahead of the listing.

Global brokerage Nomura on Wednesday gave Jio Platforms a buy rating, setting a target price of 1,340 rupees, implying an upside of 19.7% to its IPO price. The brokerage said in a report that Jio's capex cycle is largely over and there is expected to be a sharp improvement in the company's free cash flow.

Shares were last trading at 1,357 rupees.

Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's flagship company,Reliance Industries, ownsmore than a 66% stakein Jio Platforms, followed byMeta Platforms' affiliate Jaadhu Holdings that owns nearly 10% andGoogleInternational, which owns 7.7%, as per LSEG data.

Leading global funds such asBlackRock, Capital Group and GICparticipated in Jio's anchor book portion of the total fundraise, which is set aside for large institutional investors before the IPO opens for public bidding. Including anchor investors, the share offering garnered demand of $78 billion.

title: Stock futures are mixed as traders await Fed decision, Big Tech earnings: Live updates
content:
U.S. equity futures were mixed early Wednesday as investors await earnings reports from megacap technology companies and a rate policy decision from theFederal Reservedue Wednesday.

S&P 500futures inched higher andNasdaq-100futures rose 0.5%. Dow futures were 0.2% lower.

In Asia, Japan'sNikkei 225added 1.38% while the Topix rose 0.23%. South Korea'sKospisurged 6.57%, and the tech-focused, small-cap Kosdaq rose 3.09%. Australia's benchmarkS&P/ASX 200was marginally higher. Hong Kong'sHang Seng indexwas up 0.43%, while mainland China's CSI 300 gained 0.68%.

In Tuesday's regular U.S. trading, the major averagesended the session higher. Chip stocks rose again, this time powered by anannouncementfrom Broadcom that a group of banks would provide $63 billion in financing to buy the company's chips and networking solutions to be leased to Anthropic, the company behind Claude. Broadcom rose 4%, whileAdvanced Micro Devicesclimbed 5.5% andMicron Technologyrose 2.8%.

Those moves led theNasdaq Compositeto rise 1.2% on the session.

Stocks were also supported by lower oil prices, which fell following news that Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei met with thenation's top security official Mohsen Rezaeito discuss conditions for ending the war with the U.S.

On Wednesday, though, focus will turn to domestic monetary policy as the Fed wraps up its two-day policy meeting. The central bank is widely predicted to keep interest rates steady at a target rate range of 3.75% to 4%. Policymakers raised rates by a quarter percentage point at theirSeptember meeting.

According to CME's FedWatch tool, there's a roughly 92% chance that the Fed maintains the current interest rate, but some expect that Chairman Kevin Warsh will signal thatmore hikes are comingin future policy meetings. The decision on interest rates will be announced at 2:00 p.m. ET.

After the bell on Wednesday, though, investors will turn their focus to the AI trade, as "Magnificent Seven" giantsAlphabetandMicrosoftwill kick off Big Tech earnings.

Tech stocks, particularly those with exposure to the AI buildout, have struggled in recent weeks amidquestions over the technology's financing. However, Morgan Stanley's chief U.S. equity strategist,Mike Wilson, thinks that therecent recovery in tech stocksis a sign that trend may be nearing its end.

"Most of the correction is already over," he said in an appearance on CNBC's "Closing Bell" on Tuesday. "We've been in correction mode for four or five months.... the market I think has digested this very efficiently."

Shares of Chinese toymakerPop Mart, known for its popular Labubu dolls, added to their more than 30% decline so far this year, following a sharp decline in third-quarter revenue.

Shares were last down under 2%, paring losses after declining more than 6% in early trading Wednesday. They have ended in the red in nine of the past 12 sessions.

The companyreporteda 45% to 50% year-on-year drop in third-quarter revenue on Tuesday, according to a filing.

The Korea Exchange activated a buy-side sidecar on the Kospi, temporarily halting program trading, as South Korean stocks surged.

A buy-side sidecar is triggered when the Kospi 200 futures index rises 5% or more for at least one minute, stopping trading for 5 minutes.

South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix on Wednesday posted a record high quarterly profit, sharply beating estimates, and announced over $25 billion in dividends and buybacks, sending shares more than 3% higher.

SK Hynixpostedrecord quarterly revenue and operating profit, with sales exceeding 100 trillion won for the first time, as it announced plans to return about 100 trillion won to shareholders — including at least 30 trillion won in cash dividends and 60 trillion won in share buybacks and cancellations.

The chipmaker approved a third-quarter dividend of 14 trillion won, including a special dividend funded by gains from its investment in Kioxia. The company will also buyback 20 trillion won in shares, half of which will be cancelled this year.

Asia-Pacific markets traded higher early Wednesday.

Japan'sNikkei 225added over 0.74% while the Topix rose 0.32%.

TheKospigained 2.06% at open, while the small-cap Kosdaq rose 1.78%.

Australia's benchmarkS&P/ASX 200was 0.84% higher.

Asia-Pacific markets were set to open higher Wednesday, tracking U.S. stocks that rose on optimism around AI stocks, while a slide in oil prices also lifted market sentiment.

Japan'sNikkei 225was poised to gain, with the Chicago futures contract at 64,410 and its Osaka counterpart last trading at 64,420, compared with the index's previous close of 63,268.37.

Hong KongHang Seng indexfutures were at 23,093, compared with the index's last close of 23,041.32.

Australia'sS&P/ASX 200was up 0.27% in early trade.

Crude oil prices fell for the second straight session Tuesday, helped by a renewed diplomatic push to de-escalate tensions in the Middle East.

Oracle rallied 3.6% on Tuesday as it took steps tointegrate ChatGPT and Codex into appsand expand its cloud chip lineup.

Oracle is adding OpenAI's ChatGPT and Codex to its application stack, extending enterprise access to OpenAI tools. Mahesh Thiagarajan, Oracle's president of Cloud Infrastructure, told CNBC at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas that usingChatGPT"allows anybody to build an application, deploy it, manage it."

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure will add Google TPUs, OpenAI's Jalapeño chip and Cerebras hardware as customers seek more silicon options. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is set to join Oracle co-CEO Clay Magouyrk for a keynote at Oracle AI World.

Oracle shares are down 33% in 2026, and off about 54% over the past 12 months.

title: Kylian Mbappé faces China backlash as sponsors cut ties over viral meme
content:
Kylian Mbappé is facing growing fallout in China over remarks apparently referring to Mao Zedong as a dictator, with sponsors dropping the French striker and Spanish football broadcasts disrupted.

China’s state broadcaster CCTV has warned that Mbappé’s apology will ultimately be judged by his actions.

“We will listen to his words, but watch his actions even more closely,” an unnamed China Media Group representativesaidon Oct. 27, urging Mbappé, Real Madrid and La Liga to learn from the incident and mend their ways.

A day earlier, the broadcaster had suspended La Liga coverage and matches involving the French forward, while also pulling advertisements in which he appeared.

His social media accounts on Xiaohongshu and Weibo were also subsequently muted, according toRenmin Ruiping, People's Daily's online commentary platform.

Neither a resumption of broadcasts nor the lifting of the account restrictions could be independently confirmed as of Oct. 28.

The backlash followed the circulation of a clip from French program "The Bridge," in which Mbappé discussed a meme depicting his face superimposed onto Mao, the late Chinese communist party chairman and founding leader of the People's Republic of China.

In the clip, Mbappé said the funniest meme he had seen of himself showed his face superimposed onto that of “some guy—I think he’s a Chinese dictator,” according to a report by Reuters.

Reuters said it could not independently authenticate the video.

The football star has since apologized in Chinese, French and English ina statement on Xon Oct. 27, acknowledging that his comments were ill-judged and have hurt many Chinese communities around the world.

La Liga alsoissued an official statementexpressing deep regret over the hurt caused to Chinese fans by Mbappé's remarks, adding that his personal views do not represent the Spanish league's position.

The commercial fallout has also been swift.

Dongpeng Beverage,Mengniuand cheese makerMilkgroundannounced the termination of their partnerships with Mbappé, according to company statementscompiled by China.org.cn, a state-run web portal and news service.

Dongpeng’s sports drink brand Bushuila hadunveiledhim as its ambassador only in April this year.

Meanwhile, On andDiorhave also reportedly removed Chinese promotional content featuring Mbappé, although neither had announced a global termination,according to Chinese news outlet Phoenix.

The Real Madrid star had about a million followers on Xiaohongshu andWeiboeach, with Reuters reporting that four topics relating to the football star were among Weibo's top 10 searches on Oct. 27.

People’s Daily, the official newspaper of the Chinese communist party’s central committee,reinforced the criticismthrough its online commentary platform Renmin Ruiping.

The commentary argued that celebrities who cross public boundaries can become liabilities for brands, and that profiting from a market while offending its people's cherished history and culture would not be accepted.

China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman Guo Jiakun alsoaddressedthe controversy as well, noting that the ministry was aware of the reports.

"Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society," he added.

title: Trump says Iran war will end 'when I want it to' as costs reportedly balloon to $47 billion
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump has reiterated his claim that the Iran war will end "whenever I want it to," but insists that Tehran cannot have a nuclear weapon.

Speaking at a rally in Lubbock, Texas, Trump said "Somebody asked me before, 'When will the war in Iran end?' I said, 'Whenever I want it to end.'"

Trump said it "would be very quick, but we have to have an end properly,"with a "total statement" that Iran would never have a nuclear weapon.

His statement comes as the President grapples with poll numbers that are near a record low due to rising energy costs and affordability issues as the U.S. heads into the midterm elections on Nov. 3.

Currently, Trump's approval ratings stand at 32%, according toa Reuters/Ipsos pollon Monday.

Mark Zandi, Moody's Analytics' Chief Economist said on Oct. 12 that the war was costing American familiesan average of $2,000so far, where $1,100 comes from higher energy costs, $540 from higher interest rate costs, and $360 due to increased military spending.

The Iran conflict shows no sign of winding down, with Trump saying that he will soondecide whetherto "make a deal" with Iran or "finish it off."

Earlier in the month, the U.S. hadevacuated diplomatsfrom Saudi Arabia, as the New York Times reported that U.S. and Israeli militaries have drawn up specific plans for a "short but intensive" operation for strikes on Iran after the midterm elections.

An estimate by U.S. Central Command on Oct. 16,according to a report by The Hill,also revealed that the cost of the Iran war has ballooned to $47 billion, about $3 billion more than the previous numbers.

The bulk of the costs was reportedly for munitions replacements at $29 million. Washington's conflict with Iran has caused"shortfalls" in U.S. munitions,despite Trump claiming on Sept. 3 that the U.S. had "virtually unlimited" amounts of ammunition.

The massive price tag on the war does not include the costs of damaged military bases in the Middle East, which is estimated at $184 million as of June 29, according to alead inspector general reportto Congress.

This figure counts damage to U.S. diplomatic facilities in four countries — Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates—from Iranian strikes.

title: SK Hynix third-quarter profit sharply beats estimates on AI memory boost
content:
South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix on Wednesday released its third-quarter earnings results, posting a record high quarterly profit that sharply beats estimates, while announcing over $25 billion in dividends and buybacks.

Here are SK Hynix's third-quarter results compared with LSEG SmartEstimates, which are weighted toward forecasts from analysts who are more consistently accurate:

Revenue rose 327.9% from a year earlier, while operating profit climbed 632.1% year on year.

Compared with the previous quarter, revenue climbed 31.9%, while operating profit surged 37.6%.

SK Hynixpostedrecord quarterly revenue and operating profit, with sales exceeding 100 trillion won for the first time, as it announced plans to return about 100 trillion won to shareholders — including at least 30 trillion won in cash dividends and 60 trillion won in share buybacks and cancellations.

The chipmaker approved a third-quarter dividend of 14 trillion won, including a special dividend funded by gains from its investment in Kioxia. The company will also buyback 20 trillion won in shares, half of which will be cancelled this year.

SK Hynix expects HBM4 to surpass HBM3E in both shipments and revenue in the fourth quarter, as it ramps up production at its M15X facility in Cheongju, South Korea.

HBM, or high-bandwidth memory, is a type of advanced memory used alongside AI processors to handle large amounts of data. HBM4 is the sixth generation of the technology.

The company has secured long-term agreements with 14 major customers covering more than 50% of its production capacity for 2027 and 2028.

It expects memory demand to outpace supply through 2030 and plans to significantly increase investment next year.

In August, SK Hynixhad announcedplans to repurchase and cancel 40 trillion won worth of its own shares, while raising its shareholder return target to more than 50% of cumulative free cash flow generated between 2025 and 2027.

Last week, SK Hynixannouncedthat its U.S. subsidiary Solidigm would halt its review of potential pre-IPO fundraising and IPO options, citing market volatility and share price trends.

The company said it would continue to assess investment timing, scale and financing options to support Solidigm's growth and enhance shareholder value.

title: Indian investors rush to Nvidia, SpaceX, Apple as local trading apps roll out access to U.S. stocks
content:
Major Indian online investment platforms are unlocking access to U.S. stocks for millions of retail investors eager to diversify into global assets as the country's markets continue to underperform.

Earlier, access to U.S. markets and exchange-traded funds was limited to wealthier Indians, via global banks and wealth management firms.

Groww, an Indian investment platform that accounts for more than 29% of the country's 46 million active investors across stock brokerages, rolled out the U.S. equity trading feature earlier this month, Harsh Jain, chief operating officer and co-founder of the company, told CNBC.

NVIDIA,SpaceX,Apple,Alphabet,Amazon,MicronandMetaare the most popular companies among early users, Jain said, whose firm has provided access to more than 10,000 U.S. stocks, exchange-traded funds and fractional share ownership.

Zerodha, the second-largest trading platform with a 15% share of active clients as per NSE data, has also started beta testing access to U.S. stocks and plans to launch in a few weeks, the company told CNBC.

Another popular brokerage with 6.7 million active retail clients, Angel One, is also reportedly planning to launchU.S. stock tradingon its platform.

There is a "big interest" among Indians to invest in U.S. stocks, especially in tech companies, Nitin Jain, chief executive and director at Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Singapore, told CNBC. He added that "retail investors like whatever goes up," pointing to the frenzy among Indian investors for investing in crypto a few years back.

"There has always been latent demand in India for investing in global companies," Somnath Mukherjee, vice president of corporate development at Zerodha, told CNBC.

He said that the underperformance of the Indian stock market over the past few years and the lack of local artificial intelligence champions is driving the demand for U.S offerings. The depreciation of the Indian rupee against the dollar is also pushing investors "to keep a part of their portfolio in another currency," Mukherjee said.

India's benchmark stock index, the Nifty 50, has dropped nearly 13% since the start of the year while the S&P 500 has gained over 12%. Foreign investors are fleeing the country's markets, with a record$32.5 billion in outflowsin direct equities since January, as per data from Indian depository NSDL, pressuring the stock market.

With the absence of any major AI company and relatively expensive valuations, investors have picked markets such asSouth Korea and Taiwanover India, experts said.

In August, resident Indians sent over $321 millionoverseas for investing in equity and debt, up 111% from a year ago, according to the Indian central bank's data. In the financial year ended March 2026, outward remittances for investments in equity and debt stood at $2.6 billion.

While the retail outflows are a small fraction of India's currency reserves, the worry is that they rise exactly when the rupee is weak, and US markets look strong, and thereby "amplify pressure at the worst moment," Tanvi Kanchan, associate director, head of international business and strategy, Anand Rathi Shares & Stock Brokers said.

Investment now accounts for about 11.7% of total outward remittances, up from 5.8% a year ago, so Indians are shifting from spending abroad to investing abroad, Kanchan said.

The exit of foreign investors and rising energy bills due to the Iran war have alreadyhit the Indian currency, warranting the central bank to step in. Kotak's Jain cautioned that as participation increases, the Indian regulator could have "second thoughts" around allowing retail access to U.S. markets.

title: Grand jury rejects DOJ bid to indict ex-Trump WH aide Cassidy Hutchinson: Reports
content:
A federal grand jury Tuesday rejected a request by the Department of Justice to indict formerWhite HouseaideCassidy Hutchinsonover her 2022 congressional testimony about PresidentDonald Trump's conduct during the Jan. 6, 2021, mob attack on the U.S. Capitol,The Washington Postreported.

Prosecutors in the DOJ's Civil Rights Division sought to charge Hutchinson with a crime based on claims she made false statements,MS NOWsaid, citing two people with knowledge of the case.

Hutchinson told lawmakers a second-hand account about Trump angrily lunging at a security aide after being told he could not go to the Capitol that day.

Senior DOJ lawyer Neville Hedley, without naming Hutchinson in open court, on Tuesday told Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui that the grand jury in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., had rejected a requested indictment, The Post reported.

It is extremely rare for a grand jury to refuse to indict when prosecutors present evidence of alleged crimes.

But since Trump returned to the White House in January 2025, federal prosecutors in Washington have several times failed to obtain a grand jury indictment they sought.

In recent weeks, prosecutors have filed separate criminal cases in U.S. District Court in D.C. against former FBI Director James Comey and two former FBI officials with charging documents other than grand jury indictments.

In both cases, the alleged conduct occurred years earlier. Typically in such cases, prosecutors would seek a grand jury indictment.

Hutchinson testified in June 2022 to the House Select Committee that investigated the Jan. 6 Capitol riot by a mob of Trump supporters, whose attack delayed for hours the confirmation of Joe Biden's electoral victory in the 2020 election.

She said that after Trump spoke at a rally outside the White House that preceded the attack, then-White House official Tony Ornato asked her, "Did you effing hear what happened in [the president's vehicle,] The Beast?"

She testified that Ornato told her that when Trump got in the car, he was under the impression from his then-Chief of Staff Mark Meadows that they going to the Capitol, as he had claimed in his speech to supporters at the rally.

When Robert Engel, the head of Trump's security detail, said the president could not go there because the area was not secure, Trump "had a very strong, a very angry response to that," Hutchinson testified that Ornato said.

"Tony described him as being irate," Hutchinson said, noting that Trump had said something like: "I'm the effing president, take me up to the Capitol now," according to Ornato.

When Engel refused again to drive him to the Capitol, Trump "reached up towards the front of the vehicle to grab at the steering wheel. Mr. Engel grabbed his arm, said, 'Sir, you need to take your hand off the steering wheel. We're going back to the West Wing,'" Hutchinson testified.

Trump "then used his free hand to lunge toward Bobby Engel," Hutchinson said she was told by Ornato.

Correction: Neville Hedley is a senior DOJ lawyer. An earlier version misspelled his name.

title: Jim Cramer warns investors not to get fooled by the latest AI stock rally
content:
CNBC'sJim Cramerwarned Tuesday that investors may be getting ahead of themselves by declaring the artificial intelligence trade back on track.

AI-related stocks rallied for a second straight session, fueled by renewed enthusiasm for chipmakers after a group of banks andBlackstoneannounced $63 billion in financing forAnthropicto purchaseBroadcom'scomputing hardware. The gains followed Monday's rally, sparked in part byAnthropic's S-1 filing. But Cramer cautioned the renewed optimism doesn't resolve the pressures facing the data center trade, which washit hard late last week.

"I'm pleased that people feel so comfortable that tech is all good to go because there is money flowing back in," the "Mad Money" host said. "I don't think that's a reason to call all clear. I think it's a reason to look at other sectors in the economy."

Cramer's skepticism centers on three lingering risks.

First, Cramer remains concerned about smaller AI infrastructure companies, known as neoclouds, that are taking on significant debt to fund the data center build-out. Rising interest rates have intensified worries about their ability to sustain those borrowing costs. Cramer singled outCoreWeave, whose bonds haveyielded as much as 15%, along withNebiusandIren. Despite an almost 8% rebound in CoreWeave shares Tuesday, he warned that fresh negativity around CoreWeave could emerge.

"I have learned that after every positive story about anything in the data center, there will be a plethora of negative stories about something wrong, including Coreweave," Cramer said.

Second, Cramer questioned whether the Broadcom-Anthropic financing deal was as reassuring as investors believed. While the $63 billion package demonstrated that lenders were still willing to finance massive AI investments, Cramer raised concerns that Anthropic is borrowing money to buy Broadcom's technology, rather than paying for it with profits from its own business. "People don't seem to grasp that [Anthropic] got the money in the Broadcom-arranged financing deal to purchase equipment from Broadcom," he said.

Finally, Cramer said that Tuesday's calmer bond market could prove short-lived. Oil prices declined and the10-year Treasuryyield fell below 5%, easing some pressure on AI companies that need to borrow heavily to fund their data center investments. But those conditions could reverse, particularly with the Federal Reserve set to announce its latest interest rate decision Wednesday afternoon, followed by Chairman Kevin Warsh's post-meeting press conference. The midterm elections next week and potential flare-ups in the Middle East may represent additional sources of volatility.

"With the exception ofNvidia, these data center companies don't have a lot of money. So they have to borrow the money," Cramer said. "The rates are getting so high that the return is getting uncertain. That hasn't changed at all."

Cramer emphasized that he remains "an unabashed believer in the AI build-out." But until the industry's financing challenges ease, he isn't ready to declare the coast clear.

title: Landline switchover could cut people off in emergency, minister warned
content: Image source,Getty ImagesByBrian WheelerPolitical reporterPublished27 October 2026Plans to switch off the UK's traditional landline phone network could leave people in remote areas unable to contact help in an emergency, MPs have warned.Landline operators aim to complete the switch to an internet-based network instead of copper-wire cables by the end of January next year.The government and operators say the move to digital landlines will offer a more reliable service.But MPs representing remote areas of the UK urged security minister Dan Jarvis to ensure that scrapping the copper-wire network did not make their communities more vulnerable in a storm or other emergency.Unlike digital services, the traditional landline network does not rely on mains electricity and continues to work in a power cut.Labour MP Torcuil Crichton, who represents the Western Isles constituency of Na h-Eileanan an Iar, said: "Resilience is inbuilt in the islands but we have major problems with connectivity because of this move from analogue to digital phone lines."He said that "when the power goes out people don't have the phone, they don't have the internet and often they don't have a mobile signal either".Retail service providers have been giving back-up battery packs to vulnerable customers, which can keep landline phones operating for an hour or more.But Crichton said this was "simply not adequate" and that mobile phone providers "simply don't have the means to maintain or keep their signal going during storms".He urged the minister to get telecoms firms to "up their digital game" to protect places "on the edge where people are vulnerable, isolated from their neighbours, where the ambulance is an hour away and the storm is 70 miles an hour".Similar concerns were raised by MPs from the West Country and the Lake District.Markus Campbell-Savours, Labour MP for Penrith and Solway, said: "I ask the minister to imagine an elderly constituent living alone in an isolated Lake District valley where copper phone lines have been replaced by fibre."A storm takes out the power to their router in the night and by the time they wake, the modest battery back up has failed, as has the mobile mast, does the minister share my concerns that they would have no way to raise an alarm in an emergency and agree that we need a new technological solution to protect the elderly?"'We won't be able to use our phones if we have a power cut'Published22 December 2025Switchover must protect most vulnerable - MPsPublished24 March 2025Conservative MP Julian Lewis also raised concerns about the lack of a "back-up system" if digital phone services go down in the event of a cyber attack or other emergency.He told Jarvis the copper-wire network "could have given us useful levels of resilience in an emergency".Jarvis, who is spearheading the government's Be Ready campaign,which is advising people to stock up on supplies to be prepared for emergencies, said he would "look very closely" at the Tory MP's point.He also assured West Country MPs that their concerns would be addressed at a government resilience summit, which was due to take place in Cornwall next month, and promised to raise concerns about telecoms firms with the Department for Culture, Media and Sport."Our telephone networks are a vital part of our critical national infrastructure and our emergency response in weather-related crisis supports the functioning of essential services and keeping people connected when they need it most," he told MPs.The government says the switch to digital phone services is needed because the traditional analogue network is becoming increasingly unreliable.The government'sBe Ready campaign advises people,externalwho have not yet "migrated to a modern digital network" to contact their landline provider."If you are a vulnerable customer, for example if you are a telecare user, your communication provider must provide a free backâup battery unit," it adds.More information is available on the government'sdigital switchover site,external.Related topicsDan Jarvis
